configuration_summary.summary: adservice Deployment (boutique) exposes gRPC on container port 9555. The readinessProbe uses grpc on port 9555 (initialDelaySeconds 5), which matches the gRPC service. The livenessProbe uses httpGet on path / port 9555 (initialDelaySeconds 5), which is an HTTP probe against a gRPC-only server — a protocol mismatch that can cause liveness failures and abnormal restarts. Resources: requests 200m CPU/180Mi, limits 300m/300Mi.

telemetry_summary.summary: Observed: adservice pod adservice-d6c9fcc6b-d4nlb has restarted 2 times within ~90s of creation; all other boutique pods are stable with 0 restarts. Pod describe shows liveness probe (http-get on port 9555, path /) failing repeatedly (9 failures over 81s), causing kubelet to kill and restart the container (exit code 143, Terminated/Error). The liveness probe error indicates the server responds with a non-HTTP/1.x (binary/HTTP2) payload to the HTTP probe; adservice logs show matching Netty Http2Exception 'Unexpected HTTP/1.x request: GET /' errors (8 errors in 116 log lines, ~6.9% error ratio), confirming the adservice gRPC server rejects HTTP/1.x requests. Readiness probe uses grpc on 9555 and passes (pod Ready). No active metric alerts. Hypothesis (not yet confirmed): the liveness probe is misconfigured (wrong protocol for a gRPC server), i.e., liveness_probe_incorrect_protocol, causing the abnormal restart loop; the app itself appears healthy per gRPC readiness. Uncertainty: whether the probe config was recently changed or is default; no deployment YAML or alert history inspected yet.

output.reasoning: The adservice container serves only gRPC on port 9555 (readinessProbe correctly uses grpc on 9555 and passes; pod is Ready). The livenessProbe is configured as httpGet against the same gRPC-only port 9555. The kubelet's HTTP/1.x probe receives a binary HTTP/2 preface from the gRPC server, fails to parse it as HTTP, and marks the container unhealthy. After 3 consecutive failures the kubelet kills the container (exit code 143) and restarts it, producing the observed restart loop (Restart Count: 2, Killing events x3). The application itself is healthy per the passing gRPC readiness probe, so the restarts are caused solely by the liveness probe protocol mismatch.
